<p>If RequiredSymbol is used (the default) for a given symbol then that symbol must be found during the lookup or the lookup will fail returning a SymbolNotFound error. If WeaklyReferencedSymbol is used and the given symbol is not found then the query will continue, and no result for the missing symbol will be present in the result (assuming the rest of the lookup succeeds).</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Introduce relocations to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">Sym</span> in its own definition if there are any pointers formed via PC-relative address that do not already have a relocation.</p>


<p>This is useful when introducing indirection via a stub function at link time without compiler support. If a function pointer is formed without a relocation, e.g. in the definition of <span class="doxyComputerOutput">foo</span></p>


<div class="doxyProgramListing">

<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">_foo:</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  leaq -7(%rip), rax # form pointer to _foo without relocation</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">_bar:</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  leaq (%rip), %rax  # uses X86_64_RELOC_SIGNED to </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">'_foo'</span></span></div>

</div>


<p>the pointer to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">_foo</span> computed by <span class="doxyComputerOutput">_foo</span> and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">_bar</span> may differ if we introduce a stub for _foo. If the pointer is used as a key, this may be observable to the program. This pass will attempt to introduce the missing "self-relocation" on the leaq instruction.</p>


<p>This is based on disassembly and should be considered "best effort". It may silently fail to add relocations.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Clone a function declaration into a new module.</p>


<p>This function can be used as the first step towards creating a callback stub (see makeStub).</p>


<p>If the VMap argument is non-null, a mapping will be added between F and the new declaration, and between each of F's arguments and the new declaration's arguments. This map can then be passed in to moveFunction to move the function body if required. Note: When moving functions between modules with these utilities, all decls should be cloned (and added to a single VMap) before any bodies are moved. This will ensure that references between functions all refer to the versions in the new module.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Create a <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/memorybuffer">MemoryBuffer</a> covering the "linkable" part of the given path.</p>


<p>The path must contain a relocatable object file or universal binary, or (if AllowArchives is true) an archive.</p>


<p>If the path is a universal binary then it must contain a slice whose architecture matches the architecture in the triple (an error will be returned if there is no such slice, or if the triple does not specify an architectur).</p>


<p>If the path (or universal binary slice) is a relocatable object file then its architecture must match the architecture in the triple (if given).</p>


<p>If the path (or universal binary slice) is a relocatable object file then its format must match the format in the triple (if given).</p>


<p>No verification (e.g. architecture or format) is performed on the contents of archives.</p>


<p>If IdentifierOverride is provided then it will be used as the name of the resulting buffer, rather than Path.</p>


<p>Definition at line 35 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/lib/lib/executionengine/lib/executionengine/orc/loadlinkablefile-cpp">LoadLinkableFile.cpp</a>.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p><a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/record">Record</a> addresses of the given symbols in the given ExecutorAddrs.</p>


<p>Useful for making permanent records of symbol addreses to call or access in the executor (e.g. runtime support functions in <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/orc/platform">Platform</a> subclasses).</p>


<p>By default the symbols are looked up using <a href="#a69e9511c04540297d2cff38f4645a9abaa1734373fb555ce75d3e33411f9ea827">SymbolLookupFlags::RequiredSymbol</a>, and an error will be generated if any of the requested symbols are not defined.</p>


<p>If <a href="#a69e9511c04540297d2cff38f4645a9aba26a03cdefe35519715a4b6d564c9c9c7">SymbolLookupFlags::WeaklyReferencedSymbol</a> is used then any missing symbols will have their corresponding address objects set to zero, and this function will never generate an error (the caller will need to check addresses before using them).</p>


<p>Asynchronous version.</p>


<p>Definition at line 16 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/lib/lib/executionengine/lib/executionengine/orc/lookupandrecordaddrs-cpp">LookupAndRecordAddrs.cpp</a>.</p>
